title: Mina and the Shadow Stage
credit: Original story and SVG illustrations created for Axiom Play Studios with OpenAI Codex.

scenes.narrative: Mina and her younger brother Arun are making a pocket forest show. They have one paper tree puppet, a little story lamp and a fixed screen, all inside this on-screen stage. “How can one tree look tall, then small?” asks Arun. Mina leaves the lamp and screen in place. The puppet can move between them in our illustrative picture model.
scenes.alt: Mina, a girl with a long dark braid and coral shirt, and her younger brother Arun in turquoise stand at a purple curtain theatre. A paper tree silhouette waits on their little theatre screen.

scenes.narrative: The first part of the show needs a tree that seems tall enough to touch the curtain. Mina holds the paper tree upright. Arun points at the two places where it could stand. Choose one position, then predict the shadow’s size before testing. The little light and the pale screen will not move.
scenes.alt: The fixed lamp at left faces the fixed screen at right. One upright tree puppet can stand at the near-light or near-screen marker.

activity.variable: Puppet position between the fixed light and screen
fixed: Same upright paper tree puppet and size

outcomes.observation: Nearer the fixed light, the same tree puppet makes a larger shadow on the screen.
Nearer the fixed screen, the same tree puppet makes a smaller shadow on the screen.

activity.comparison: Compare the saved trials: where was the puppet, and how large was its shadow? Only the puppet position changes. With this point-like light and fixed screen, moving the same puppet toward the light enlarges the shadow; moving it toward the screen makes it smaller. The ray diagram is an illustrative model.

scenes.narrative: Now the story visits a tiny grove far away. The paper tree itself will stay the same size. “Could its shadow look smaller?” Arun asks. Mina can move only the puppet. Try one of the two positions and choose a prediction. The screen will keep the observed shadow still so you can look closely.
scenes.alt: Mina and Arun consider a small tree shadow for the grove. The same upright puppet stands between an unmoved lamp and screen.

scenes.narrative: Arun asks to see the towering forest once more. Mina brings the same paper tree back between the fixed lamp and screen. A repeated trial can help them check what they noticed. Choose a position and predict again. You can use Try again to keep both observations and compare them.

scenes.narrative: The curtain is ready for the pocket forest show. Mina knows how one tree puppet can make a towering shadow near the light and a smaller shadow near the screen. Arun remembers the repeated trials and the two observations. Their little forest can seem to grow and shrink while the lamp and screen stay still. The siblings take a bow together.
scenes.alt: Mina and Arun take a bow beside their purple paper-puppet stage. A tall tree silhouette fills the theatre screen, ready for another forest story.

prompts.question: What moved between the two shadow trials?
prompts.answer: Only the upright tree puppet changed position. The lamp and screen stayed fixed.

prompts.question: Where did the tree puppet make a larger shadow?
prompts.answer: Nearer the fixed light. Nearer the fixed screen it made a smaller shadow.

prompts.question: How might Arun feel when the little tree makes a large shadow?
prompts.answer: He might feel surprised, curious, excited or something else. Share what you notice.

prompts.question: What could happen in your own pocket forest story?
prompts.answer: Invent a story together. You can choose a large tree, a small grove, or another idea.
